planTheory.hypothesis: Sunny can achieve unaided spelling recall of the 10 silent-letter words by test day if given scaffolded-to-hidden recall progression, while the 10 high-frequency words only need recognition/read-aloud fluency, not spelling drills; simultaneously, varying the practice mechanic (stampede vs letter-rush) while holding target words, difficulty, and evidence contract constant will reveal which delivery mechanic Sunny prefers per the open engagement theory.
planTheory.intervention: Follow the canonical learning-cycle node contracts.
supportCriteria: Majority-correct hidden-word recall on silent_letters words confirms unaided spelling readiness for the test.
Strong completion/accuracy in one mechanic route versus the other reveals a clear engagement preference to reuse in future sessions.
Fluent visible-read and pronunciation performance on high-frequency words confirms that group needs no further spelling drilling.
reviseCriteria: Partial recall difficulty is high but hidden recall is roughly half-correct: schedule one more short targeted practice session on missed words before Friday.
One mechanic route shows much lower completion/accuracy than the other: prefer the stronger mechanic for the next session's silent_letters practice.
High-frequency words show fluency gaps: add a supported read-aloud pass next session before assuming the group is settled.
falsifyCriteria: Child cannot recall most silent_letters words unaided even after both practice routes: hypothesis that this session's dosage is sufficient is falsified; escalate to a dedicated remediation session before test day.

Child disengages or shows high frustration in both stampede and letter-rush routes: falsifies that mechanic variation alone will surface a usable preference; consider theme variation instead next time.

Child cannot read or pronounce high-frequency words despite visible support: falsifies the assumption that this group only needs light fluency checks; treat as a decoding gap requiring different instruments.
